title: SAML SSO: IdP-specific integration playbook for RBAC v2, audit logging, and admin controls
creator: Priya Nair
description: Consolidate IdP-specific compatibility notes, verification steps, and mitigation patterns for Okta, Azure AD (Entra), Google Workspace, and Ping Identity with respect to RBAC v2, enhanced audit logging, and admin control surfaces. This ticket produces a playbook for engineering, an integration checklist for solutions engineering, and a test-suite matrix for QA. The goal is to reduce onboarding friction for enterprise customers and close known swallow/attribute-mapping gaps that cause admin/control regressions and audit inconsistencies.
compatibility_summary: Okta: stable SAML assertions, supports attribute-level mapping and custom claims. Known quirks: SLO behavior in multi-spa setups, intermittent NameID format variations.
Azure AD (Entra): robust federation with claims transformation via policies. Known quirks: group claims truncation and paged group API required for large orgs.
Google Workspace: lightweight SAML implementation, limited group claim support; often requires a separate provisioning sync for robust RBAC mapping.
Ping Identity: enterprise-grade flexibility via adapters and transformer pipelines; quirks: non-standard attribute names and metadata refresh cadence differences.
known_quirks_and_mitigations: Group claim truncation (Azure AD): mitigation - prefer SCIM provisioning or paged group API retrieval; implement fallback to direct user membership lookup via directory sync.
NameID format mismatch (Okta): mitigation - accept multiple NameID formats (email, transient, persistent) and normalize before RBAC mapping.
Missing group claims (Google Workspace): mitigation - document requirement for either SCIM or 'Include in SAML assertion' setting; provide admin guide steps.
Custom attribute namespaces (Ping): mitigation - add configurable attribute name mapper in SAML adapter and provide default mappings for common Ping deployments.
SAML Logout edge-cases: mitigation - treat SLO as advisory; implement session expiry+audit marker and optional SLO webhook for downstream services.
Clock skew and assertion validity failures: mitigation - document recommended NTP drift tolerances and support configurable AssertionTimeOffset in our SAML handler.
Metadata refresh timing: mitigation - add jittered metadata refresh and manual refresh endpoint in admin console.
rbac_v2_integration_notes: RBAC v2 expects stable identity.subject and identity.source_id across sessions; ensure SAML NameID or mapped persistent attribute is used as stable key.
Map IdP groups to RBAC role bindings via a two-step process: 1) attribute extraction, 2) canonicalization and role resolution; include fallback rules for missing groups.
Support both user-attribute role grants and group-based grants. Document precedence (explicit user grants override group grants).
Provide a dry-run mode in admin console to preview role resolution given a sample SAML assertion.
audit_logging_requirements: Log original SAML assertion identifier (sha256) and the normalized subject (non-PII truncated), for traceability.
Emit audit events for: assertion validation failures, attribute-to-role mapping decisions, admin role changes triggered by SSO mappings, SLO events.
Ensure audit entries include actor, timestamp (UTC), request-id, and affected resource; correlate with session tokens for forensic reconstruction.
Retention guidance: default 90 days for high-volume orgs, configurable per-enterprise (compliance may require 1+ years).
test_plan: Create per-IdP SAML sample assertions covering NameID=email|persistent|transient and group claim patterns.
Automated CI matrix: run integration tests (assertion parsing, map->RBAC assignment, audit event emission) against mocked IdP endpoints for Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping.
End-to-end smoke tests using real dev Okta tenant and Azure AD test tenant in CI nightlies; include provisioning sync tests (SCIM).
Negative tests: expired assertions, invalid signature, missing required attributes, truncated group payloads - verify failure modes and audit logs.
Load tests: simulate SSO login bursts during enterprise onboarding (10k requests/min) to validate assertion parsing throughput and KV cache behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Per-IdP checklist completed and reviewed: attribute mapping, default mappings, UI guidance added to admin console.
Automated tests added to CI matrix for each IdP; green in nightly runs.
Audit events emitted for all major mapping/validation outcomes and visible in Console logs with sample entries.
Documentation (Confluence + Admin help) published and linked from onboarding flows.
Security review completed and sign-off from InfoSec.
implementation_notes: Add configurable attribute name mapper with default presets (okta, azure, google, ping).
Expose 'AssertionTimeOffset' and 'AcceptNameIDFormats' flags in SAML connector config with safe defaults.
Instrument assertion parsing path with tracing spans and token-level correlation IDs.
Provide a CLI tool for solutions engineering to generate example assertions for customer repros.
SCIM vs SAML guidance: recommend SCIM for large orgs where group claim truncation is observed; implement clear error message in UI.

risks_and_open_questions: Risk: Large orgs with >1500 groups still may hit token size limits for SAML. Question: should we auto-fallback to SCIM or surface guidance only?
Risk: Non-standard IdP attribute names may require ongoing maintenance; propose maintaining mapping presets per major IdP only.
Open question: default retention for audit logs for enterprise customers - legal/compliance to advise.
